item.text: IBAC reported on its oversight of Victoria Police since becoming fully operational in early 2013.
item.support: This report provides a focused account of IBAC’s key police oversight activities

item.text: It covered prevention projects, reviews of police investigations and the progress and outcomes of IBAC investigations.
item.support: reviews of Victoria Police investigations – both reviews of individual cases and reviews that highlight systemic issues

item.text: A delegated inquiry found serious negligence in handling human source information and failures to follow policy, while making no finding of unlawful behaviour.
item.support: found negligence of a high order in the management of human source information by Victoria Police

item.text: IBAC recorded 20 statutory recommendations to Victoria Police, addressing matters including human sources, subpoenas, victims of crime assistance and oversight of prosecutors.
item.support: To date, IBAC has made twenty section 159 recommendations to Victoria Police
item.section: Progress on recommendations arising from previous investigations

item.quote: In his final report, Mr Kellam found negligence of a high order in the management of human source information by Victoria Police and he concluded that Victoria Police had failed to act in accordance with appropriate policies and guidelines.
This matter highlighted a systemic issue: the significant authority granted to often junior police prosecutors operating with little or no oversight.
